audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] read Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Lissandra, Aurora, Aurora — exactly packet.levelChart.
audit.why: The content chart matches the kit. Ice Shard is 725 and Ring of Frost is 450 against Aurora's 900 Q and 825 E, so levels 1-5 belong to Aurora and Lissandra has to spend an 80-mana, 24-second Glacial Path just to reach her. Level 6 is Lissandra's: Frozen Tomb is a 550-range stun on an enemy or an untargetable, invulnerable, self-healing window on herself. First item onward is Aurora's again against a 120-second ultimate. 49.07% over 1345 games is exactly one level swinging an otherwise even lane.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side = Aurora, phases[4].side = Lissandra, phases[5..6].side = Aurora, ratings 6/6/6/6/4/6/6, every affected why rewritten in the same proposal. content win[] needed no edit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike ladder carried no numbers and spikes[2] named Riftmaker while report[8] prescribes Luden's into Sorcerer's.
audit.why: Lissandra's ladder is entirely readable from the kit: Ice Shard falls from 7s to 3s across ranks, Glacial Path from 24s to 12s, Ring of Frost sits at 10s, and Frozen Tomb is 120/100/80. The 24-second Glacial Path at rank 1 is the single widest punish window in the lane and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: Spikes rebuilt on those numbers; spikes[2] regrounded on 'your first item' rather than picking a side of the item contradiction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page had no ability interactions — every field was the Aurora template with 'Glacial Path (Claw)' pasted in. Three real interactions were absent, one stated fact was wrong, and Aurora's E was again called a 'knockback-slow'.
audit.why: enemyKit R: 'If cast on Lissandra, she encases herself in dark ice, healing herself while becoming untargetable and invulnerable' — flags untargetable and heal. Dumping a rotation into that is the single most expensive mistake available in this matchup, and it also makes Grievous Wounds relevant. enemyKit W: Ring of Frost is a 450-range self-centred root, which is the ability that actually kills you once she closes — not Glacial Path. enemyKit E: the claw is created first and she reactivates to travel to it, so it is a telegraphed reposition, and it is her only escape. ownerKit E: damage and slow, then Aurora hops backward — no knockback, and that backward hop is exactly the distance that breaks a 450 root.
audit.corrected: The untargetable self-cast is now stated in tldr, winCon, loading, mid, late, breakdown.late, report[5] and spikes[3]. Ring of Frost's 450 root is the spacing anchor throughout. Glacial Path is framed as a 24-second commitment that is also her only exit. E restated correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (catalogue defect 3), and dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' off Glacial Path.
audit.why: Glacial Path is 24 seconds at rank 1, not fifteen — the advice was understating the best window in the lane by nine seconds.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Glacial Path 24s to 12s, Ring of Frost 450 at 10s, and Frozen Tomb 120/100/80; the invitation is 24 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Lissandra was called he/his in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, ahead, loading, breakdown.wave, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[2].t, dosFull[2].t, phases[0].why, phases[5].why and four report entries.
audit.why: champ-gender.js lists lissandra as female; the owner is 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page is Lissandra.
audit.corrected: Fixed, with the sentences regrounded in her kit rather than pronoun-swapped in place.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid described the enemy-cast Frozen Tomb as 'a hard root' and the self-cast as merely 'a defensive out'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'the target is frozen solid, stunning it'. A stun and a root are not interchangeable for a player deciding whether a spell will still come out. And the self-cast is untargetable and invulnerable, not just defensive.
audit.corrected: Restated as a 550-range stun, and the self-cast described by what it actually does.

notes: All seven chart rows read 'Skill' in the full layer while content win[] already matched packet.levelChart; flipped the sides with paired ratings and rewritten whys in one proposal. The page named Glacial Path as the matchup-defining ability, but the kit says the thing that kills you is Ring of Frost — a 450-range self-centred root on a 10-second cooldown — while Glacial Path is a 24-second, 80-mana commitment that is also her only escape. Both are now stated with numbers. The biggest gap was Frozen Tomb's self-cast: untargetable, invulnerable and self-healing, which means a full Aurora rotation dumped into it is thrown away, and which is also why Grievous Wounds matters in a long game. Neither had ever appeared on the page. content mid also called the enemy-cast Frozen Tomb 'a hard root'; Riot's text says stunning, and the distinction decides whether a queued spell still comes out. dosFull[2].d advertised a 'fifteen-second invitation' against a 24-second cooldown, understating the best punish window in the lane. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit. Fifteen misgendered fields fixed. spikes[2] named Riftmaker against report[8]'s Luden's line; regrounded on 'your first item'. 'Glacial Path (Claw)' is the AbilityName (Effect) convention and was left intact per the brief. As with the other Aurora matchups, packet.suspectNames flags 'The Weirding's' and the page also uses 'Twin Drift'; the kit file carries no ability names for Aurora, so I could not verify either and avoided both.
